title: The Spiritual & Aesthetic Significance of Peacock Jharokhas in Indian Homes
excerpt: Discover how the peacock motif and traditional royal Jharokhas bring divine grace, positive vibrational energy, and architectural grandeur to modern living spaces.
author: Murli Prasad
content: In Indian cultural heritage and Vedic lore, the peacock (Mayura) is revered as a symbol of divine royalty, grace, protection, and eternal renewal. When sculpted into a traditional Rajasthani Jharokha (arched balcony frame) with Kutchi Lippan clay relief and shimmering mirrors, it transforms an ordinary living wall into a sacred architectural centerpiece.

According to Vastu Shastra principles, placing peacock-inspired handcrafted murals in the North-East or East orientation of a home draws vibrant positive energy, balances planetary influences, and invites spiritual tranquility into the household.

At Murli Creations, each Peacock Jharokha is hand-sculpted over several days. Fine clay coils are rolled by hand to form the flowing crest and feather eyes, embedded with authentic mirrors that reflect natural sunlight during the day and warm lamp glow in the evening.

title: Sacred Vastu Guidelines for Placing Lippan Art & Mandalas at Home
excerpt: A complete guide on the optimal wall orientations, color harmonies, and sacred directional energies when placing handcrafted Mandalas and clay relief murals.
author: Murli Prasad
content: The sacred geometric Mandala represents the cosmic universe, balance, and centered inner peace. When combined with the earthy resonance of clay and reflective mirrors in Lippan art, it creates a powerful focal point in any room.

To maximize positive cosmic flow, Vastu experts recommend placing Circular & Lotus Mandalas on North-East (Ishanya) walls for spiritual growth and clarity, or on East walls for health, vitality, and fresh morning solar energy.

Avoid hanging sacred Mandalas directly below staircases or facing bathrooms. Instead, position them at eye level in prayer rooms (Mandir), foyer entryways, or living rooms where positive vibrations can radiate freely throughout the home.

title: The Ancient Mud & Mirror Craft of Kutch: Heritage Preserved with Devotion
excerpt: Journey into the centuries-old art of Lippan Kaam from the white desert of Kutch, and learn how authentic artisan techniques keep the craft alive.
author: Murli Family
content: Originating from the pastoral Rabari and Mutwa artisan communities of Gujarat's Kutch region, Lippan Kaam was traditionally created on the mud walls of circular Bhunga huts to keep interiors cool during scorching summers and reflect faint lantern light at night.

The soul of true Lippan art lies in the delicate raised clay relief (Kaam) crafted using organic clay mixtures, cured adhesives, and hand-cut mirrors (Aabhla). No two handcrafted pieces are ever identical, giving every mural a distinctive, living character.

At Murli Creations, we honor this timeless legacy by preserving traditional mud-and-mirror sculpting techniques on reinforced, moisture-sealed wooden panels tailored for modern urban apartments and villas.

title: Studio Guide: How to Care for & Clean Your Handcrafted Lippan Art
excerpt: Simple, essential maintenance tips to keep your clay relief motifs and mirrors gleaming for decades without damaging the organic paint finish.
author: Master Craftsman Team
content: Handcrafted Lippan wall art is remarkably durable when treated with basic care. Because our panels are sealed with high-grade protective matte and gloss topcoats, they resist humidity and ambient dust easily.

To dust the raised clay ridges, use a soft, dry microfiber cloth or a gentle painting brush once every two weeks. For mirrors, lightly dab a cotton swab with standard glass cleaner or dilute water to restore sparkling brilliance without rubbing the surrounding clay.
Always hang your artwork using the pre-installed heavy-duty metal hardware provided on the back, and avoid exposing the piece to direct rainfall or harsh outdoor moisture.
